images.title: Rectangle and square
images.purpose: Show that a rectangle has equal opposite sides and four right angles, and a square has four equal sides and four right angles.
images.composition: A long rectangle on the left and a square on the right with wide space between them.
images.exact_structure: Left: one rectangle 6 units long and 3 units wide in teal #0072B2; the 2 long sides carry 1 tick mark each and the 2 short sides carry 2 tick marks each; a small square corner sign at each of the 4 corners. Right: one square of side 3 units in amber #E69F00; all 4 sides carry 1 tick mark each; a small square corner sign at each of the 4 corners. Exactly 2 shapes, 8 corner signs.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
tick marks that differ from the count stated
images.takeaway: A square has every property of a rectangle.
images.description: A teal 6 by 3 rectangle with tick marks on opposite sides and four right angle signs, beside an amber square of side 3 with four equal tick marks and four right angle signs.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the equal sides and the right angles of each shape.

image_decisions.why: Placing the two shapes side by side with marks shows what they share.
